test_cases.scenario: Log in with a valid email and password
preconditions: Active account user@example.com exists with password Valid#Pass1
User is logged out and on the login page
test_cases.expected_result: The user leaves the login page and the header shows the logged-in state (account name and a 'Logout' option)
test_cases.notes: Merged duplicates LG-01 and LG-02; replaced 'logged in successfully' / 'works as expected' with observable outcomes.

test_cases.scenario: Log in with a valid email and a wrong password
preconditions: Active account user@example.com exists with password Valid#Pass1
User is on the login page
test_cases.expected_result: An error message is displayed on the login page and the user remains on the login page and is not logged in (no logged-in header state)

test_cases.scenario: Submit the login form with both fields empty
preconditions: User is on the login page
test_cases.expected_result: An error or required-field indication is shown for the empty fields and the user remains on the login page and is not logged in (no logged-in header state)

test_cases.scenario: Log in with an email that is not registered
preconditions: User is on the login page
test_cases.expected_result: An error message is displayed and the user remains on the login page and is not logged in (no logged-in header state)

test_cases.scenario: Submit with email filled and password empty
preconditions: User is on the login page
test_cases.expected_result: An error or required-field indication is shown for the password field and the user remains on the login page and is not logged in (no logged-in header state)

test_cases.scenario: Submit with password filled and email empty
preconditions: User is on the login page
test_cases.expected_result: An error or required-field indication is shown for the email field and the user remains on the login page and is not logged in (no logged-in header state)

test_cases.scenario: Log out from a logged-in session
preconditions: Active account user@example.com exists with password Valid#Pass1
steps: Log in with the test data credentials
test_cases.expected_result: User is logged out and redirected to the homepage

test_cases.scenario: Back button after logout does not restore the logged-in session
preconditions: Active account user@example.com exists with password Valid#Pass1
User is logged in and viewing their account page
test_cases.expected_result: The account page is not shown in a logged-in state after reload; the header shows the logged-out state
test_cases.notes: Common logout risk not covered by the original suite.

review_findings.description: LG-01 and LG-02 both test a valid login with the same steps.
Expected results 'logged in successfully', 'Login works as expected', 'Error shown' and 'Error' cannot be verified.
review_findings.action: Rewritten with observable outcomes in TC-LOGIN-001..003.

review_findings.description: LG-05 'Test login' has the step 'Test the functionality' and expected result 'Works correctly'; it tests nothing identifiable.
review_findings.action: Removed; its intent is covered by TC-LOGIN-001.

review_findings.description: No case for an unregistered email.
Empty-field validation only tested with both fields empty.
No boundary cases (password length, lockout attempts); the limits are not known from the tests.
review_findings.action: Not added; recorded as a coverage gap pending Q-2.

review_findings.description: Logout is only tested for the redirect, not session invalidation.

gaps.description: Boundary cases for password length and lockout
Email format validation, case sensitivity, session timeout
gaps.reason: No requirement available (Q-1); not added to avoid inventing behaviour

gaps.description: Negative login paths are tracked under REQ-002 and REQ-003
gaps.reason: REQ-001 is the happy path only; its rejections are separate inferred requirements

coverage_summary.notes: The original 6 cases reduce to 4 (1 kept, 3 improved; LG-02 merged and LG-05 removed), plus 4 new cases for unregistered email, single empty fields and post-logout session. All cases are assumption-based because requirements were reverse-engineered from the tests; supplying the login requirement (Q-1) and the password and lockout rules (Q-2) would enable boundary coverage.

requirements.text: A user can log in with a valid email and password
Login with invalid credentials is rejected with an error
Login with empty fields is rejected with an error
A logged-in user can log out and is redirected to the homepage
